WASHING Ton, May 10.


City of Washington, May 10.


In pursuance of a notice given to the Republican Members of Congress generally, eighty-two Members of Congress convened In the Senate Chamber at the Capitol, viz.


SENATORS.—Messrs. Anderson, Brent, G. W. Campbell, Condit, Crawford, Cuts, Gregg, Howell, Leib, Pope, Robinson, Smith, S. N. TAFT, Taylor, Turner, Varnum, Worthington.


REPRESENTATIVES.—Messrs. Bartlet, O. Hall, Harper, Green, Seaver, Turner, Fisk, Shaw, Mitchell, Sage, Sammons, Boyd, Condit, Morgan, Richardson, Hyonan, Anderson, Bard, Brown, Crawford, Davis, Findley, Lacock, Lyle, Piper, Smith, Smith, Ringgold, Wright, Bassett, Warren, N. J. Clay, Dawson, Gholson, Goodwyn, Hives, Taliaferro, McCoy, Nelson, Newton, Peasants, Aston, Cochran, King, Pickens, Butler, Calhoun, Earle, Moore, Winn, Bibb, B. Hall, Group, H. Clay, Desha, Johnson, McKee, Ormsby, New, Grundy, Rhea, Morrow, Poindexter, Jennings, Sever—65.


Total 80.


The meeting was opened at seven o'clock.


On motion of Mr. Smith, the Hon. J. B. VARNUM was appointed Chairman, and J. M. JOHNSON Secretary of the meeting.


Mr. Findley having briefly explained the purpose of the meeting—


On motion of Mr. Anderson, of Tennessee it was


Resolved, That the meeting do now proceed to recommend proper persons as candidates to fill the offices of President and Vice President of the U. States, for the term of four years from the 4th day of March next.


The meeting first proceeded, on motion of Mr. Anderson, to ballot for the candidate for the Presidency; and Messrs. Mitchell and Sage being appointed Tellers, it appeared, on counting the ballots, that the votes were as follows:


For JAMES MADISON, 50.


No other person being voted for,


The meeting then proceeded, in like manner, to ballot for suitable person to be supported for the Office of Vice President for the term. On counting the ballots, it appeared that there were


For JOHN LANGDON 81
For ELBRIDGE GERRY 10


Scattering


On motion of Mr. Campbell of Tenn. it was then


Resolved, As the sense of this Meeting that JAMES MADISON, of the state of Virginia, be recommended to the people of the U. S. as a proper person to fill the office of President, for four years, from the 4th of March next: And that JOHN LANGDON, of the state of N. Hampshire, be recommended as proper person to fill the office of VICE-PRESIDENT for the same term.


Resolved, That in making the foregoing recommendation, the members of this meeting have acted only in their individual characters, as citizens & that they have been induced to adopt the measure from deep conviction of the importance of union to the republicans, throughout all parts of the country.


On motion of Mr. Findley, the following gentlemen were appointed a Committee of correspondence and arrangement, viz.


Mr. Cuts of N. Hampshire, Mr. Varnum of Massachusetts, Mr. Howell of R. Island, Mr. Robinson of Vermont, Mr. Sage of N. York, Mr. Condit of N. Jersey, Mr. Smith of Penn., Mr. Ringgold of Maryland, Mr. Burwell of Virginia, Mr. Pickens of N. Carolina, Mr. Taylor of S. Carolina, Mr. Crawford of Georgia, Mr. Anderson of Tenn., Mr. Pope of Kentucky, Mr. Morrow of Ohio, Mr. Poindexter of Louisiana, Mr. Poindexter of Mississippi, Mr. Jennings of Indiana.


And the meeting adjourned.


J. B. VARNUM, Chairman
J. M. JOHNSON, Sec'y.


A letter was received from Mr. P. L. Langdon, of the House of Representatives of Pennsylvania, of his regret at being confined by indisposition and asking to be permitted to vote by proxy for James Madison. The vote by proxy was not deemed admissible.


THE BOARD.—The letter of the Secretary of the Treasury, in this day's paper, which we particularly request the attention of the opposition editors, precludes the necessity of any further remarks from us on this subject. It is one on which our friends need feel no uneasiness and however high may have been the Federal tone, we predict that this plain official statement of fact, will reduce it below hard. Mar. LyL.
